title: Replication, in-sync replicas and what a broker failure costs

videos.script: Three machines hold the same sales. {{three}} One of them takes the writes. It is called the leader. The other two copy everything it receives, as fast as they can. {{copy}} At four in the afternoon, the leader's disk dies. {{dies}} A few seconds later, one of the copies is the leader. The tills never stopped, and nobody in the shop noticed. {{moves}} That is the promise of replication. This lesson is about its small print. {{print}} A copy that has fallen behind is not really a copy. So Kafka keeps a list of the ones that have not. {{isr}} A producer chooses how many copies must hold a sale before it is told yes. {{acks}} And when too many machines are lost, Kafka has to choose. It can stop. Or it can carry on, and forget what it had. {{choice}} You will run three nodes on your own machine, and kill them on purpose, one at a time. {{kill}}
